qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Fifth-largest bank in Spain with dominant branch and deposit density in Andalusia and Castile & León following the Liberbank integration. High switching costs in sticky rural and regional retail deposit accounts provide a low-cost funding base, supporting a rebound in ROTE to 10.4% in 2024 and adjusted ROTE of 12.1% in 2025.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 4 (CAP = 5, REJECT). Regional retail banking in Spain is subject to intense commoditization, high regulatory/political intervention (such as the Spanish extraordinary bank tax), and cyclical net interest margin compression as ECB policy rates decline. Under the Mauboussin framework, commercial banking is anchored in Tier 4 with rapid return fade (baseline CAP 5-10 years). Operating in a saturated Spanish domestic market with low economic growth and demographic headwinds in core rural regions, CAP cannot exceed 5 years.
qualitative.evidence: Historical capital returns have been modest and cyclical: ROTE was 4.7% in 2023, recovering to 10.4% in 2024 and 9.1% standard / 12.1% adjusted in 2025 as higher interest rates boosted net interest income. Cost-to-income ratio stands at ~44-46%. Balance sheet is heavily weighted toward domestic residential mortgages (~60% of loans), where pricing is largely commoditized against Santander, BBVA, and CaixaBank. Post-merger governance friction and domestic Spanish sovereign exposure further curtail long-term predictability.
